chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hashim Abu Saeed Al-Mukari, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Five prayers that you may pray at any time: the prayer of the eclipse, the prayer upon the deceased, the prayer of Ihram, the missed prayer, and the prayer of Tawaf; from dawn until the sun rises, and after Asr until night.
ai.seo_question: What are the five prayers that can be performed at any time in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that these five specific prayers—eclipse, funeral, Ihram, missed (Qada), and Tawaf—possess the unique legal status of being valid at any time, even during periods when prayer is typically disliked (Makruh) or prohibited (Munha). Notably, the inclusion of 'Salat al-Ihram' highlights the Shia view of the initial intention as a distinct prayer act, while the Tawaf prayer's timing reflects the practical need to complete rituals before the sun's elevation interferes with other obligations.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Hashim Abu Saeed Al Mukary, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Five Salāts, you can pray these during every time – The Salāt for the eclipse, and the Salāt upon the deceased, and Salāt of (wearing) Al-Ihraam, and the Salāt which is missed out, and Salāt of the Tawaaf – from the dawn to the emergence of the sun, and after Al-Asr up to the night’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn Hashim ibn Sa‘id af-Mukariy from abu Basir from who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

There are five Salah (prayer) which you can perform anytime you want. Such Salah (prayer) are because of eclipse, for a deceased, for Thram, for making up a missed one, for Tawaf from dawn to sunrise and after al-‘Asr until night.’”
